chunks: And it has been narrated: that

"The Ka'bah was only named Ka'bah because it is square. It became square because it is aligned with al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, and it is square. And al-Bayt al-Ma'mur became square because it is aligned with the Throne, and it is square. And the Throne became square because the words upon which Islam was built are four, and they are: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar."

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامُ: Islam, the religion built upon these four formulas
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ: al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, the oft-frequented heavenly house
key_terms.كَعْبَةً: the Ka'bah, the sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is the Ka'bah described as square in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a symbolic cosmological relationship between the Ka'bah, al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, and the Throne. It presents their square form as connected to the four foundational formulas of dhikr upon which Islam is said to be built.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"The Ka'bah was named 'Ka'bah' because it is cubical in shape. It became cubical because it is directly beneath the Bayt al-Ma‘mur, which is also cubical.
The Bayt al-Ma‘mur became cubical because it is directly beneath the Throne (‘Arsh), which is cubical as well.
The Throne is cubical because the foundational words upon which Islam is built are four: Subhan Allah (swt) (Glory be to Allah (swt)), Alhamdulillah (Praise be to Allah (swt)), La ilaha illa Allah (swt) (There is no god but Allah (swt)), and Allahu Akbar (Allah (swt) is the Greatest)."
